caption:
1-week itinerary for Mallorca 🇪🇸🌞🌊

I recommend splitting the trip into two parts: beaches on the east coast and the small towns in the north 🫶🏻

1️⃣ When visiting the east coast and its beaches, it is easiest to rent a car (from the airport in Palma) because the bus connections are pretty inconvenient and slow in this part of the island. I recommend staying in this area (for example, in Cala d’Or) for about 3-5 nights. There are dozens of pretty little beaches along this coast, and I recommend visiting as many as you can, but a few of my favorites were Caló del Moro, Cala s’Almonia ja Cala Llombards.

2️⃣ After the east coast, you can return the car to the airport, after which you can spend about half a day exploring Palma, the capital and biggest city of Mallorca.

3️⃣ From Palma, you will continue your trip to Sóller, where I recommend you stay for 2-3 nights. I don’t think you need a car here because the buses are pretty good, and driving and parking in these small towns may be difficult. 

You should visit at least Port de Sóller (beach town of Sóller) and the cute nearby villages of Valldemossa and Deià. If you have the time, I recommend also visiting Fornalutx. You can visit all these by bus from Sóller 🚌

caption: Mallorca looks easy on a map but it doesn’t feel easy when you’re actually driving it. Most trips go wrong because people treat it like a flat island and try to do Palma, Sa Calobra, Formentor and the east coast all from one base. The reality is very different. Tramuntana roads are slow, winding and draining, parking fills up early in the north and Formentor has restrictions in peak season. You don’t just lose time, you lose energy, and that’s why trips start to feel heavy halfway through. The fix is simple but most people ignore it. Start in Palma or the southwest for an easy arrival, then move your base and group the north properly so you do Formentor, Tramuntana and Sa Calobra in one phase. After that shift east and slow everything down. Flat roads, short drives, beach days that actually feel like a break. Mallorca isn’t hard, bad routing is. #mallorca #mallorcatravel #spaintravel #travelplanning #traveltips

caption:
I’ve lived in Mallorca for years, and these are my honest ratings of some of the island’s most popular beaches. ❣️

My opinion has changed over time — and so has my idea of quality time at the beach. I still remember the excitement of visiting for the first time and wanting to see as much as possible in the shortest time. But now I see that rushing from spot to spot often takes away from the experience, and also adds pressure to the places we visit.

For years, there have been growing concerns about overtourism in Mallorca and the “crowd effect” created by social media, where certain beaches become photo stops rather than places to truly enjoy. Many of these spots are home to fragile ecosystems, so it’s worth slowing down and visiting more consciously.

That can be as simple as researching a place before you go, respecting local rules, leaving no trace, and taking your rubbish with you (many natural beaches have no bins). If you see litter, even better — pick it up. 🌿

Parking at some beaches is also very limited and expensive, so public transport can sometimes be the easier and more stress-free option (also will help you save up to 30€/day on parking🥶

I’ll keep sharing useful videos on conscious ways to visit Mallorca, so follow along if you’d like to see more — and comment which beaches you’d like me to rate next. I may keep my absolute hidden gems to myself… but there are still many incredible places to share.
